deep.reconstruction: This page contains no mathematics. It continues the anatomical setup of Riemann's fragment on the mechanics of the ear, posthumously published by Henle as 'Mechanik des Ohres' (Zeitschrift für rationelle Medicin, 3. Reihe, Bd. 29, 1867). The previous page described the ossicular apparatus in two parts. The first is a rigid body made of hammer and anvil (malleus and incus), which rotates about an axis. The second is a piston, the stirrup (stapes), which articulates with that body and presses on the fluid at the oval window. One end of the rotation axis is the short process of the incus, fixed to the posterior wall of the tympanic cavity by the incudo-tympanic joint. This page completes the description of the other end. The long (anterior) process of the malleus, surrounded only by soft tissue, projects into a fissure between the anterior-superior end of the tympanic ring and the petrous part of the temporal bone (the petrotympanic, or Glaserian, fissure). There it lies in a groove of the ring. Riemann adds the caveat that this holds at least for the ear of the newborn. He then adopts Henle's orientation convention for describing the ossicles' position relative to the tympanic cavity. One imagines the cavity rotated so that the rotation axis of the malleus-incus body runs horizontally from back to front and the oval-window plane stands vertical. In modern terms this fixes a body-adapted coordinate frame: the x-axis is the hinge axis and the vestibular window lies in a vertical plane. This simplifies the later lever analysis of how the malleus handle's rotation is transmitted to the stapes. A struck-out word ('Weiter') follows. The left margin carries the editorial or compositor instruction 'Kein Absatz' ('no paragraph break'). A long vertical stroke fills and cancels the remaining blank space. The mechanical or mathematical modelling, including the conditions on stapes pressure and the energy partition of a sound wave at a stretched membrane, begins on the following pages.

results.what: Anatomical description of the malleus-incus rotation axis: the short incus process is anchored posteriorly; the long (anterior) malleus process lies in the petrotympanic fissure in a groove of the tympanic ring (newborn ear).
results.modern_name: Axis ligament / rotation axis of the ossicular chain (Helmholtz-style 'Axenband')
results.usually_credited_to: Classical otology; Henle's anatomy texts and Helmholtz, 'Die Mechanik der Gehörknöchelchen und des Trommelfells' (1868)

results.what: Orientation convention: imagine the tympanic cavity rotated so the ossicular rotation axis is horizontal (posterior to anterior) and the oval window is vertical.

deep.surprise_reason: Purely descriptive anatomy with an explicitly cited convention of Henle. The passage belongs to Riemann's already-published fragment 'Mechanik des Ohres' (1867, and Gesammelte Werke). It contains no mathematical content.
